Subject: Cross-border controls and DPF evidence — initial RFI

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking our RFI. As part of our vendor due diligence we're collecting evidence related to international transfers and technical safeguards for processors handling patient-derived data. We need the following (targeting a response by end of month):

- A concise summary of how requests are routed by region (including automatic fallback behavior if a region is saturated).
- KMS key residency options and whether customer-managed keys can be pinned to a region; an export-control summary for keys.
- Evidence of continuous prefix/KV caching controls and how cached entries are limited to regional nodes (if applicable).
- A list of subprocessor regions (cloud infra + third parties) and whether any tokenization or pseudonymization occurs before external handoff.
- Audit log schema sample (redacted) showing per-request model variant, node/region, and decision to fallback to alternative model.
- Retention and deletion procedures for model inputs and produced embeddings; where backups are stored and for how long.
- Our legal team also requested a redline of your standard DPA annex with notes on cross-border mechanisms (DPF/SCCs or equivalent).

Please attach any operational evidence (diagrams, logs, playbooks) and indicate items that require an NDA or in-person review.

Best,
Soma Patel
Head of Privacy Programs
Medique Health

--
Attachment: medique_rfi_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Soma Patel <soma.patel@medique.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medique.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border controls and DPF evidence — initial RFI

Hi Soma — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a consolidated evidence pack and a redline of the DPA annex. High level:

- Routing: requests are routed by geo-policy with region affinity; automatic fallback uses pre-configured model variants in alternate region pools and is logged with reason codes.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) in supported regions; keys can be scoped to a region but backup/replication behavior depends on the chosen KMS provider — we will include options.
- Caching: KV/prefix caches have TTLs, per-customer namespaces, and are pinned to serving region unless explicit multi-region routing is enabled.
- Subprocessors: list attached. No external vendor receives raw input without pseudonymization controls for regulated datasets (we'll flag specifics in evidence).
- Audit logs & retention: sample schema + retention policy attached. We keep request metadata for 90 days by default; embeddings retention configurable.

I'm attaching an initial pack: redwood_dpf_operational_evidence_v1.pdf and a draft DPA annex tailored for Medique (dpa-annex-draft-medique.docx). The KMS diagram is included (key_rotation_kms_diagram.png).

If acceptable, let's schedule a 45-minute working session next week with DevSecOps to walk the diagrams and answer any technical questions. Proposed times: Tue 2029-04-30 09:00 PT or Wed 2029-05-01 11:00 PT.

Notes: some items (detailed sample audit lines, full logs) require a data-sharing addendum / NDA for production-level extracts. I've marked those sections in the PDF.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_dpf_operational_evidence_v1.pdf; dpa-annex-draft-medique.docx; key_rotation_kms_diagram.png

Olga — quick answers:

- BYOK: When a customer supplies a CMK in a supported region we do not replicate the CMK to another region by default. Replication is disabled unless the customer selects cross-region backup during onboarding. We'll include a one-page table for each KMS provider outlining default replication behavior.
- Encryption segmentation: keys and disk volumes are scoped to tenant namespaces; hosts use per-tenant encryption contexts for at-rest separation.

I'll add the exact wording you can paste into the annex regarding "KMS residency and replication defaults".

-Rishi

Soma — thanks again for the list and the patience while we pulled materials together. Attached is a consolidated evidence pack and the annex redline. Highlights and next steps below:

- Attachments (attached to this message): redwood_dpf_operational_evidence_v1.pdf; dpa-annex-draft-medique.docx (redline, two commercial options flagged); key_rotation_kms_diagram.png.
- Routing & fallback: our runtime routes by geo-policy; fallback triggers are logged (reason codes included in sample audit lines). See PDF pages 6-8.
- KMS residency: BYOK keys are not replicated across regions by default. Customers can opt-in to cross-region replication during onboarding; if Medique requires enforced regional-only backups and key replicas, we offer that as a contractual option (see Option B in annex).
- Caching: KV caches are per-tenant and pinned to the serving region unless multi-region routing is explicitly configured. TTLs and namespace scoping are documented in the evidence pack.
- Logs & retention: sample audit schema included; full raw extracts require an NDA. Default retention: 90 days for request-level metadata; embeddings retention is configurable and can be set to 0 days on request.
- Commercial note: Grace has added a price appendix illustrating the delta for reserved capacity + region-pinning. We can inline this in the annex if you prefer.

Next steps: please confirm which annex option Medique prefers (Option A: standard routing + SCCs; Option B: strict region pinning + Reserved capacity pricing). We are available for a technical walkthrough — Tue 2029-04-30 09:00 PT is still possible (we can expand to 45 min) or Wed 2029-05-01 11:00 PT. If you confirm Option B we'll include the commercial addendum in the DPA redline.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through diagrams and the KMS table.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
